# New house renderings coined in odyssey-021 (4.742–847)

These follow the same table format as conventions.md's "House renderings" section, for merging
into that table.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| εἴδωλον (of the dream-phantom Athena creates, 796 and passim) | "phantom" | "phantom" | "image", "likeness" (both lose the standing supernatural sense the word will carry at its later recurrences, e.g. of the shades in the underworld), "ghost" (wrong register — this εἴδωλον is a living construct sent by a goddess, not a spirit of the dead), "wraith" |
| τὴν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενον προσέφη εἴδωλον ἀμαυρόν (reply-formula, 824 = 835, verbatim) | "Her answering addressed the dim phantom:" | "In answer the dim phantom said to her:" | "the faint wraith" (loses "phantom" as the fixed noun above), "shadowy" for ἀμαυρόν (reserved imagery is kept literal: "dim, faint, indistinct" is ἀμαυρόν's plain sense, not itself disputed) |
| φίλη τροφὸς Εὐρύκλεια (Eurycleia's standing name-periphrasis, 742) | "the dear nurse Eurycleia" | "her dear nurse Eurycleia" | "old nurse" (drops φίλη's warmth), "nurse Eurycleia" alone (drops φίλη) |
| νύμφα φίλη (Eurycleia's affectionate address to Penelope, 743) | "Dear bride" | "Dear lady" | "my dear child" (over-interprets; νύμφη is literally "young wife, bride", kept literal in `l`), "my dear" alone (loses the address form), "dear daughter" (Penelope is not Eurycleia's daughter) |
| Ἀτρυτώνη (cult-title of Athena, 762) | "Atrytone" | "Atrytone" (+ note: traditionally "the Unwearied", ἀ- + τρύω, but the formation is irregular and the sense not fully certain) | "the Unwearied" or "the Untiring" as if certain (silently picks one guess); "tireless one" |
| ὀνειρείῃσι πύλῃσιν ("at the gates of dreams", 809) | "at the gates of dreams" | "at the gates of dreams" | "in a dream-gate" (loses the plural), "dreaming at the threshold" (too free); kept literal since Book 19 later elaborates the image into gates of horn and of ivory |

## Judgment calls not entered as new table rows

- **τὴν/τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε applied with a feminine object** (742, 830): conventions.md fixes
  this reply-formula only for the masculine τόν ("Him then in turn addressed" / "Then … spoke to
  him in turn"). Here the formula recurs twice with the feminine τήν (once of Eurycleia
  addressing Penelope, once of Penelope addressing the phantom). I translated it by the same
  pattern with "her" for "him", on the model of how the table already gives both τόν/τήν forms of
  the sibling formula τὸν/τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα. I did not add a separate table row since it is
  the identical formula, gender-matched to its object; a reviewer may want to fold this explicitly
  into the existing row 127 wording ("τὸν/τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε").
- **ὣς φάτο applied to a female speaker** (758, of Eurycleia): the table fixes "ὣς φάτο" as
  "So he spoke" / "So he spoke", presumably because it had so far only closed a male speaker's
  words. Here I rendered it "So she spoke," keeping the same skeletal construction but adapting
  the pronoun, on the model of how the table already tracks separate masculine/feminine variants
  of other speech-formulas (e.g. ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας/φωνήσασ'). Flagged for the reviewer's confirmation
  that this is the intended house practice rather than a fixed, un-adapted "he".
